work.title: Readela 0.3.0: final correction and performance validation of draft pull request 9 after the owner's third review
work.ownerAuthorization: Owner instruction of 2026-10-11 continuing ENT-246 after the owner's review of head d9d4542 on the real sites. It authorizes the bounded work in scope.inScope on the existing branch feat/ent-240-readela-0.3.0, its tests, performance measurements, documentation and evidence, commits and their push to that branch, an accurate description of draft pull request 9, and a fresh local unpacked Chrome build for owner review. departuresFromAcceptedDecisions.note: The instruction of 2026-10-11 knowingly changes points of DEC-141 and DEC-142, which were read again on 2026-10-11. The instruction is the owner's and later; it governs this work. No Decision recording these points existed in Personal OS when this record was written, and this work does not write there.
points: DEC-141 authorizes no background service, and DEC-142 allowed a keyboard action only without one. The instruction removes the fixed key and allows a minimal event-driven background component to receive one browser-managed command that has no default key.

DEC-142 names the popup's language as Saved place, Save or Update, Return and Clear, with the current and total status. The instruction renames the feature to Bookmark, with Bookmark or Update, Return and Remove, and shows the total only.
DEC-136 and the Product Brief name line spacing 1.6, 1.9 and 2.2. The instruction replaces them with 1.5, 1.75 and 2.0.
departuresFromAcceptedDecisions.dueBeforeIntegration: The owner's record of these points in Personal OS; see openItems OPEN-3.

inScope: This record, committed first on the existing branch from baseCommit.
Line spacing: the choices become Original, 1.5, 1.75 and 2.0; a stored 1.6, 1.9 or 2.2 is read as 1.5, 1.75 or 2.0. The preferences format and its version are unchanged.

The feature's visible language becomes Bookmark: the popup section shows the total only, with Bookmark or Update, Return and Remove, one short helper line and the state of the shortcut. Internal names stay where a rename would only be churn. Targeting, matching, storage and return are unchanged.

Claude sidebar indicator, from the cause observed on the site: most rows of its list carry an address that does not name the conversation the page shows. Where the site marks the row of the conversation shown, a one-way fingerprint of that row's address path is kept with the place, as an optional eleventh value, so the row can be recognised later. It is written when the reader bookmarks or updates, and once more when the list first shows which row is this conversation's and the stored value is missing or different. No title, label or address is stored.
The sidebar indicator becomes about 8 by 14 CSS pixels on both sites, with placement that may differ by site and nothing else.

Inline code and tokens under Paper and Night: one stronger Readela-owned treatment on both sites, including the element ChatGPT uses for inline code, which is not a code element; that element also keeps its own font under Readela Sans. Complete code blocks and tables are not reopened.
The key listener for Alt+Shift+S and everything that mentions it are removed.

One browser-managed command with no default key: a commands entry in the manifest and a background component that only listens for it and passes one message to the content script of the active tab, which performs the same Bookmark or Update as the popup and shows the brief emphasis. The popup shows the assigned shortcut or that none is set, and opens the browser's own shortcut settings. No permission is added.

A measured performance and resource audit of the content script, the popup and the background component in Chrome, with representative cases repeated in Firefox; removal of avoidable recurring or repeated work where measurement shows it; a repeatable measuring script kept with the tests, with no cost in the packaged extension.
Tests, fixtures, documentation and dated evidence made necessary by the above; a fresh local unpacked Chrome build for owner review; an accurate description of pull request 9.

externalCapabilities.note: Load-bearing behaviour of the browsers and of the two supported sites, verified before the contract was frozen. The sites were read in the owner's signed-in browser on 2026-10-11: element names, attribute names, computed styles, geometry and counts only; no conversation text, title or address was recorded and nothing was typed or sent. The browsers were probed with a throwaway extension in the versions the tests use.

items.capability: Chrome: a command declared without suggested_key is unbound until the user assigns a key at chrome://extensions/shortcuts; commands.getAll reports its shortcut as an empty string; the commands key needs no permission; commands.onCommand is delivered to the extension's service worker with the active tab, which carries no address without the tabs permission; an extension page can open chrome://extensions/shortcuts with tabs.create and no permission. Chrome has no commands.openShortcutSettings, commands.update or commands.onChanged.
items.authority: developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/commands and MDN's note on openShortcutSettings, read on 2026-10-11. Probe in Chrome 154.0.8037.98: getAll returned the command with an empty shortcut; tabs.create opened chrome://extensions/shortcuts; a command dispatched to the service worker's listener arrived with a tab that has an id and no address; openShortcutSettings, update and onChanged were undefined.
items.probe: The end-to-end suite checks the manifest of the built Chrome package, the popup's shortcut line and its settings action, and delivers the command to the service worker's listener.

items.capability: Firefox: Manifest V3 runs background.scripts as a non-persistent event page and does not support background.service_worker; a command without suggested_key has an empty shortcut; commands.openShortcutSettings (Firefox 137) opens the browser's Manage Extension Shortcuts; commands.onCommand passes the tab from Firefox 126; the browser validates a shortcut and refuses a single letter. The minimum version declared in the manifest is 140.
items.authority: MDN manifest.json/background and API/commands pages and the browser-compat-data for commands, read on 2026-10-11. Probe in Firefox 157.0: getAll returned an empty shortcut; commands.update accepted Alt+Shift+9 and refused B with the browser's own message; commands.onChanged reported the change; openShortcutSettings resolved and opened about:addons; runtime.getBackgroundPage returned the event page.
items.probe: The end-to-end suite assigns a shortcut through the browser's own commands.update, checks the popup's line, and calls the background component's handler.

items.capability: A key press sent through the automation protocol does not reach the browser's own shortcut handling in either browser.
items.authority: Probe in Firefox 157.0: with Alt+Shift+9 assigned, the key pressed on an ordinary page did not fire the command. Chrome's protocol delivers keys to the page only.
items.probe: None possible; the path from a real key to the command is the browser's and is left to the owner's review.

items.capability: Claude: most rows of the sidebar's list are a[data-row-main-button] whose href is /cowork/cse_<id>, while the conversation such a row opens is shown at /chat/<uuid>; the two identifiers are not derivable from each other in the page. Rows of older conversations carry /chat/<uuid>. The row of the conversation shown carries aria-current="page". A row link fills its row (left edge 8px, text 6px further in) inside a list that clips at 4px.
items.authority: Observed on 2026-10-11: 24 of 28 conversation rows had the first form; clicking one showed /chat/<uuid> with that row as the only aria-current link; no attribute of the row or its ancestors held the uuid; the build of d9d4542, installed there, removed a test attribute from an unsaved row within a second, so its marking was running and found no key to match.
items.probe: The Claude fixtures carry rows of both forms with aria-current on the row of the conversation shown; the end-to-end suite marks, updates, removes, re-renders and reloads them.

items.capability: ChatGPT: inline code in a reply is span[data-markdown-copy="inline-code"] with a translucent background, 6px corners and a dir attribute; it is not a code element. Sidebar row links sit 10px inside their row.
items.authority: Observed on 2026-10-11 in a conversation with 31 such spans and no inline code element; under the build of d9d4542 with Readela Sans the spans had the reading font.
items.probe: The ChatGPT fixture renders inline code the same way; the end-to-end suite checks its colours under both themes and its font under Readela Sans against Original.

notObserved: A real key assigned in the browser's shortcut settings reaching the command, in either browser.

risk.targetedVerification: Manifest contract tests: permissions stay ["storage"], one command with no suggested key, a background entry of one file per browser, the web-accessible resources unchanged. A source test that the background component holds no timer, no network call and no listener but the command's, and that the content script listens for no key. Unit tests of the stored place with and without the row fingerprint and of the spacing migration. End-to-end checks that the command saves through the same path as the popup, that nothing is sent anywhere, that storage holds only the two objects without readable text, titles or addresses, that only the rows of bookmarked conversations are marked on both sites and that Off removes every mark and stops the page being observed. Measurements of idle work, of interaction and of a long run, before and after any change made for them.
